raw_response:
Alright, let me think through this year's plan. I've been doing this 20 years, so most of it I already know — but every year's a little different.

---

**My thinking:**

I've got 20 mu, all in wheat-maize rotation. That's how everyone around here farms. My two kids and my wife help when they can, but my older boy works in town most of the year, so for busy times — wheat harvest into maize planting especially — I usually pay a neighbor with a combine and planter. Can't afford to lose days in that turnaround, it's maybe 5 days between cutting wheat and getting maize in the ground.

For **wheat**, I planted in early October last fall already — winter wheat, I used Jimai variety seed I bought from the agricultural supply store, about 15 kg/mu seeding rate. Before planting I put down compound fertilizer as base — roughly 40 kg of 15-15-15 per mu, plus another 10 kg of urea. The extension people say you should soil test and split more carefully, but honestly I just do what's worked. Come spring at jointing I'll topdress another 15 kg of urea per mu, maybe a bit more if the field looks pale. That gets me around 18-19 kg total N per mu for wheat, which is where I've landed after years of trying.

Wheat needs water. I'll irrigate maybe 3 times with the tube well — once before winter to settle it, once at jointing in March, and once at grain filling in May. Each irrigation costs me real money in electricity and diesel, so I watch the rain. If spring rains come good, I might skip one. Last year I irrigated 4 times and spent too much, yield wasn't really higher. Expecting around 480 kg/mu — last year was 460, conditions look okay so far.

For **maize**, I'll plant right after wheat harvest in mid-June, Zhengdan 958 or Xianyu 335 — whatever the shop has fresh seed for. Hire the planter, about 40 yuan/mu. I apply compound fertilizer at planting, around 40-45 kg/mu of a maize-type compound, then topdress urea at big trumpet stage, maybe 15 kg/mu. Total N around 16-17 kg/mu for maize. 

Maize often doesn't need much irrigation here because of summer rains, but if July is dry I'll water once or twice. I also spray herbicide after planting — atrazine mix, one pass — and maybe an insecticide for corn borer if I see damage.

I don't skimp, but I don't go crazy either. My neighbor Old Wang puts on way more fertilizer, doesn't get more yield. Another neighbor tried cutting back, his yield dropped. I'm in the middle where it makes sense.
